paragraphs: Iron Mountain Incorporated, a Delaware corporation ("IMI"), was founded in an underground facility near Hudson, New York in 1951 where it stored business records. Today, we are a global leader in information management services, and we are trusted by more than 240,000 customers in 61 countries, including approximately 95% of the Fortune 1000, to help unlock value and intelligence from their assets through services that transcend the physical and digital worlds. Our broad range of solutions address their information management, digital transformation, information security, data center and asset lifecycle management ("ALM") needs. Our longstanding commitment to safety, security, sustainability and innovation in support of our customers underpins everything we do. We currently serve customers across an array of market verticals — commercial, legal, financial, healthcare, technology, insurance, life sciences, energy, business services, entertainment and government organizations.

We are listed on the New York Stock Exchange (the "NYSE") and are a constituent of the Standard & Poor's 500 Index, the Morgan Stanley Capital International ("MSCI") REIT index and the FTSE EPRA Nareit Global Real Estate Index. As of December 31, 2025, we were number 567 on the Fortune 1000. We have been organized and have operated as a REIT beginning with our taxable year ended December 31, 2014.

Our strategy is to be the leading partner to our more than 240,000 customers by providing a broad range of end-to-end solutions leveraging our strong reputation for security and chain of custody, decades-long relationships built on trust, and global footprint and operational scale. With leadership positions in physical records management, digital solutions, data center, and asset lifecycle management, Iron Mountain serves as a key global partner for enterprises.
Our key strategic priorities are outlined below.

•We are focused on driving volume growth, while also capitalizing on revenue management opportunities as we enhance the value we are providing customers through our expanded suite of global and integrated services.

•We are a leading global provider of physical records management services and will seek to enhance our position in higher-growth markets such as Central and Eastern Europe, Latin America, Asia, the Middle East and Africa.

•We are focused on supporting our customers' digital transformation needs as they navigate a complex regulatory environment and seek to gain access to their dark data. Our strategy is underpinned by our persistent focus on best-in-class customer experience as we continue to deliver innovative solutions, such as Insight Digital Experience Platform ("DXP"), to help our customers better leverage data and drive improved efficiency.
•We provide our digital solutions offering globally to customers across an array of market verticals.

•We are focused on growing our data center operating portfolio by leasing unsold capacity to hyperscale customers across various global markets. We are also focused on completing construction and commencing data center leases entered into in prior periods.

•As of December 31, 2025, we operated 31 data centers across 21 global markets, either directly or through unconsolidated joint ventures. In addition, we had leased approximately 97% of the existing 488 megawatt ("MW") capacity of our data centers. With a total potential capacity of 1,340 MW in land and buildings currently owned or operated by us, we are among the largest global data center operators.

ALM: Providing asset lifecycle management capabilities, which are both economic and environmentally sustainable •We are a global ALM provider and are focused on broadening our customer base and increasing our penetration with existing customers through cross-selling initiatives, expanded capabilities and select tuck-in acquisitions.
•As of December 31, 2025, we operated 34 facilities across 8 global markets. PROJECT MATTERHORN

In 2025, we completed our investments in Project Matterhorn, a global program designed to accelerate the growth of our business ("Project Matterhorn"), which we announced in September 2022. Project Matterhorn investments focused on transforming our operating model to a global operating model. Project Matterhorn enabled the development of a solution-based sales approach that allowed us to optimize our shared services and best practices to better serve our customers' needs. As part of this, we invested to accelerate growth and to capture a greater share of the large, global addressable markets in which we operate. We incurred approximately $574.4 million in Restructuring and other transformation costs related to Project Matterhorn since its inception. Costs were comprised of (1) restructuring costs, which included (i) site consolidation and other related exit costs, (ii) employee severance costs and (iii) certain professional fees associated with these activities, and (2) other transformation costs, which included professional fees such as project management costs and costs for third party consultants who assisted in the enablement of our growth initiatives. Total costs related to Project Matterhorn during the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023 were approximately $195.9 million, $161.4 million, and $175.2 million, respectively.

The amount of revenues derived from our business segments and other relevant data, including financial information about geographic areas and product and service lines, for the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023, are set forth in Note 10 to Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements included in this Annual Report.

We face many risks. If any of the events or circumstances described below actually occur, we and our businesses, financial condition or results of operations could suffer, and the trading price of our debt or equity securities could decline. Our current and potential investors should consider the following risks and the information contained under the heading "Cautionary Note Regarding Forward-Looking Statements" before deciding to invest in our securities.
Failure to execute our strategic growth plan may adversely impact our financial condition and results of operations.

As part of our strategic growth plan, we expect to invest in our existing businesses, including records and information management storage and services businesses in our higher-growth markets, data centers, digital solutions, ALM business and other complementary businesses, and in new businesses, business strategies, products, services, technologies and geographies. These initiatives may involve significant risks and uncertainties, including:

•our inability to maintain relationships with key customers and suppliers or to execute on our plan to incorporate the digitization of our customers' records and new digital information technologies into our offerings;

•failure to achieve satisfactory returns on new product offerings, acquired companies, joint ventures, growth initiatives or other investments, particularly in markets where we do not currently operate or have a substantial presence;
•our inability to identify suitable companies to acquire, invest in or partner with; •our inability to complete acquisitions or investments on satisfactory terms;

IRON MOUNTAIN 2025 FORM 10-K Part II OVERVIEW PROJECT MATTERHORN

In 2025, we completed our investments in Project Matterhorn, a global program designed to accelerate the growth of our business, which we announced in September 2022. Project Matterhorn investments focused on transforming our operating model to a global operating model. Project Matterhorn enabled the development of a solution-based sales approach that allowed us to optimize our shared services and best practices to better serve our customers' needs. As part of this, we invested to accelerate growth and to capture a greater share of the large, global addressable markets in which we operate. We incurred approximately $574.4 million in Restructuring and other transformation costs related to Project Matterhorn since its inception. During the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, we incurred approximately $195.9 million and $161.4 million, respectively, in Restructuring and other transformation costs related to Project Matterhorn. Costs were comprised of (1) restructuring costs, which included (i) site consolidation and other related exit costs, (ii) employee severance costs and (iii) certain professional fees associated with these activities, and (2) other transformation costs, which included professional fees such as project management costs and costs for third party consultants who assisted in the enablement of our growth initiatives.
GENERAL RESULTS OF OPERATIONS - KEY TRENDS

•Our organic storage rental revenue growth is primarily driven by revenue management in our Global RIM Business segment, where we expect volume to be relatively stable in the near term, as well as by growth in our Global Data Center Business segment, primarily driven by lease commencements.

•Our organic service revenue growth is primarily driven by new and existing digital offerings, traditional records management services and services in our asset lifecycle management ("ALM") business, all of which we expect to grow in the near term and benefit our organic service revenue growth in 2026.

•We expect continued total revenue and Adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization ("EBITDA") growth in 2026 as a result of our focus on new product and service offerings, cross-selling opportunities, innovation, customer solutions and market expansion in line with our growth strategies.

Our revenues consist of storage rental revenues and service revenues and are reflected net of sales and value-added taxes. Storage rental revenues, which are considered a key driver of financial performance for the storage and information management services industry, consist primarily of recurring periodic rental charges related to the storage of materials or data (generally on a per unit basis) that are typically retained by customers for many years and of revenues associated with our data center operations. Service revenues include charges for related service activities, the most significant of which include: (1) the handling of records, including the addition of new records, temporary removal of records from storage, refiling of removed records, customer termination and permanent withdrawal fees, project revenues and courier operations, consisting primarily of the pickup and delivery of records upon customer request; (2) secure shredding of sensitive documents and the subsequent sale of shredded paper for recycling, the price of which can fluctuate from period to period; (3) the decommissioning, data erasure, processing and disposition, and recycling or sale of IT hardware and component assets; and (4) digital solutions, including the scanning, imaging and document conversion services of active and inactive records, consulting services and the sale of software as a service, including our Digital Experience Platform.

Cost of sales (excluding depreciation and amortization) consists primarily of labor, including wages and benefits for field personnel, facility occupancy costs (including rent and utilities), data center pass-through power costs, transportation expenses (including vehicle leases and fuel), other product cost of sales and other equipment costs and supplies. Of these, labor and facility occupancy costs are the most significant. Selling, general and administrative expenses consist primarily of wages and benefits for management, administrative, IT, sales, account management and marketing personnel, as well as expenses related to communications, travel, professional fees, bad debts, training, office equipment and supplies.

paragraphs: Iron Mountain Incorporated, 一間設立於紐約州霍頓附近的地下設施的特拉華州公司（"IMI"），於1951年成立，當時用來存放商業記錄。今天，我們是資訊管理服務的全球領導者，並被超過24萬名位於61個國家的客戶所信賴，包括約95%的《財富》1000大企業，協助他們透過跨越實體與數位世界的服務，從其資產中挖掘價值與智慧。我們廣泛的解決方案可滿足其資訊管理、數位轉型、資訊安全、資料中心與資產生命週期管理（"ALM"）的需求。我們長期以來對安全、安全、永續性與創新對客戶的承諾，是我們一切行動的基礎。我們目前服務的客戶來自多樣化的市場垂直領域 — 商業、法律、金融、醫療、科技、保險、生命科學、能源、企業服務、娛樂與政府機構。
我們在紐約證券交易所（"NYSE"）上市，並為標準普爾500指數、摩根士丹利資本國際（"MSCI"）REIT指數與富時羅素EPRA Nareit全球不動產指數的成分股。截至2025年12月31日，我們在《財富》1000大企業中排名第567名。我們自2014年財稅年度結束後，已組織並運作為REIT。
我們的策略是成為超過24萬名客戶的領導夥伴，透過提供廣泛的端到端解決方案，善用我們在安全與鏈條 custody 方面的強大聲譽、建立在信任上的數十年關係，以及全球足跡與運營規模。在實體記錄管理、數位解決方案、資料中心與資產生命週期管理方面擁有領導地位，Iron Mountain 為企業提供關鍵的全球夥伴。
我們的關鍵戰略優先事項如下。
• 我們專注於推動營收成長，同時也把握收入管理的機會，隨著我們透過擴展的全球整合服務，提升對客戶所提供的價值。
• 我們是物理記錄管理服務的全球領導供應商，並致力於在成長較快的市場如中東歐洲、東歐、拉丁美洲、亞洲、中東與非洲地區強化我們的市場地位。
• 我們專注於協助客戶應對複雜的法規環境，並取得其暗數據的數位轉型需求。我們的策略建立在持續專注於最佳客戶體驗的基礎上，並持續提供創新解決方案，例如洞察數位體驗平台（"DXP"），以幫助客戶更有效地運用數據，並提升作業效率。
• 我們將數位解決方案提供給來自多樣化市場垂直領域的全球客戶。
•我們致力於透過將未售出的容量出租給跨各全球市場的超規模客戶，來擴大我們的資料中心營運 portfolio。我們也致力於完成建設並啟動先前期間所簽訂的資料中心租賃。
•截至2025年12月31日，我們在全球21個市場運營了31個資料中心，或是透過未合併的合資企業直接運營。此外，我們已出租約97%的現有488 megawatt ("MW") 資料中心容量。由於我們目前擁有或運營的土地和建築物總潛在容量為1,340 MW，我們是全球最大的資料中心運營商之一。
ALM: 提供資產生命週期管理能力，這些能力既經濟又環境可持續 •我們是全球ALM服務供應商，致力於透過交叉銷售計畫、擴展能力及選擇性收購，來擴大客戶羣並提高現有客戶的佔有率。
•截至2025年12月31日，我們在全球8個市場運營了34個設施。PROJECT MATTERHORN

2025年，我們完成了對Project Matterhorn的投資，這是一個全球性計畫，旨在加速我們業務的成長 ("Project Matterhorn")，我們在2022年9月宣佈了這個計畫。Project Matterhorn的投資重點在於將我們的營運模式轉型為全球營運模式。Project Matterhorn使我們能夠發展出以解決方案為導向的銷售方式，讓我們能優化共享服務和最佳實踐，以更好地服務客戶需求。作為其中一部分，我們投資以加速成長，並在我們運營的大型全球可接觸市場中佔據更大的市場份額。自Project Matterhorn啟動以來，我們產生了約5.744億美元的重組及其他轉型成本。這些成本包括 (1) 重組成本，其中包括 (i) 站點整併及其他相關退出成本，(ii) 員工人員離職成本，以及 (iii) 與這些活動相關的某些專業費用，以及 (2) 其他轉型成本，其中包括專業費用，例如專案管理費用及協助我們實現成長計畫的第三方顧問費用。2025年12月31日財年、2024年及2023年的Project Matterhorn相關成本總計約為1.959億美元、1.614億美元及1.752億美元，分別。
截至2025年12月31日財年、2024年及2023年，我們各業務分部及其他相關資料所產生的收入，包括地理區域及產品與服務線的財務資訊，請參閱本年度報告所附的財務會計彙編附註第10點。

IRON MOUNTAIN 2025 FORM 10-K 第二部分 總覽 專案MATTHORN

2025年，我們完成對專案MATTHORN的投資，這是一個全球性計畫，旨在加速我們業務的成長，我們於2022年9月宣佈此計畫。專案MATTHORN的投資重點在於將我們的營運模式轉型為全球營運模式。專案MATTHORN使我們得以發展出以解決方案為導向的銷售方式，讓我們能優化共享服務與最佳實務，以更好地服務客戶需求。作為此計畫的一部分，我們投資以加速成長，並在我們所經營的大型全球可接觸市場中取得更大的市場佔有率。自專案MATTHORN啟動以來，我們已產生約5.744億美元的重整及其他轉型成本。在2025年12月31日結訖的會計年度，我們分別產生約1.959億美元及1.614億美元的重整及其他轉型成本。成本包含（1）重整成本，包括（i）據點整併及其他相關離職成本、（ii）員工遣散費用及（iii）與這些活動相關的某些專業費用，以及（2）其他轉型成本，包括專業費用，如專案管理費用及協助我們啟動成長計畫的第三方顧問費用。
總體營運結果 - 關鍵趨勢
•我們的內生儲存租賃收入成長主要由全球RIM業務分部的收入管理所驅動，我們預期在近期內存儲量相對穩定，同時也由全球資料中心業務分部的成長所驅動，主要由租賃開始使用所帶來。
•我們的內生服務收入成長主要由新舊數位產品與服務、傳統記錄管理服務以及資產生命週期管理（"ALM"）業務中的服務所驅動，我們預期這些業務在近期內將持續成長，並有助於2026年的內生服務收入成長。
•我們預期2026年總收入及調整後營業收入（"EBITDA"）將持續成長，這是因為我們專注於新產品與服務的推出、跨銷售機會、創新、客戶解決方案及市場擴張，符合我們的成長策略。

本公司營業收入包含儲存租賃收入及服務收入，並以扣除銷售及增值稅後之金額列示。儲存租賃收入被視為儲存及資訊管理服務產業財務表現的關鍵驅動因素，主要包含與儲存材料或資料（通常以單元為單位）相關之定期租賃費用，這些資料通常由客戶保留多年，以及與我們資料中心運營相關之收入。服務收入包含與相關服務活動相關之費用，其中最主要者包括：(1) 處理記錄，包括新增記錄、暫時從儲存中移除記錄、重新歸檔被移除之記錄、客戶終止費用及永久撤回費用、專案收入及快遞運營，主要為應客戶要求所進行之記錄取件與送達；(2) 安全粉碎敏感文件，並隨後出售粉碎紙張以進行回收，其價格會因期間而有所波動；(3) 離營、資料清除、處理及處置，以及資訊科技硬體及零組件資產之回收或出售；(4) 數位解決方案，包括對活躍及非活躍記錄進行掃描、影像處理及文件轉換服務、諮詢服務及軟體即服務之銷售，包含我們的數位體驗平台。
銷售成本（扣除折舊及攤銷）主要包含人工費用（包括現場人員之工資及福利）、場地佔用成本（包括租金及電力）、資料中心轉嫁電力成本、運輸費用（包括車輛租賃及燃料）、其他產品銷售成本及設備費用與消耗品。其中，人工費用及場地佔用成本為最主要之項目。銷售、一般及行政費用主要包含管理、行政、資訊科技、銷售、客戶管理及市場營銷人員之工資及福利，以及與通訊、差旅、專業費用、呆帳、培訓、辦公設備與消耗品相關之費用。

我們面臨許多風險。若下列所描述的事件或情況實際發生，我們與我們的業務、財務狀況或營運成果可能會受到影響，並導致我們的債務或權益證券交易價格下跌。我們的現有與潛在投資者在決定投資我們證券前，應考慮下列風險及「謹慎聲明有關未來展望陳述」標題下的資訊。
未能執行我們的戰略成長計畫可能會對我們的財務狀況及營運成果造成不利影響。
根據我們的戰略成長計畫，我們預期會投資於我們現有業務，包括在高成長市場中我們的記錄與資訊管理儲存及服務業務、資料中心、數位解決方案、ALM業務及其他補充性業務，以及新業務、業務策略、產品、服務、技術與地理區域。這些計畫可能涉及重大風險與不確定性，包括：
•我們無法維持與關鍵客戶與供應商的關係，或無法執行我們將客戶的記錄數位化與新數位資訊技術整合至我們產品與服務的計畫；
•未能在新產品、收購公司、合資企業、成長計畫或其他投資中取得滿意的回報，特別是在我們目前未經營或未有重大存在市場的情況下；
•我們無法識別適合收購、投資或合作的公司；•我們無法在滿意的條件下完成收購或投資。
